gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on August 28?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 28 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data is unavailable or missing for the observation period, Weather Underground will be used as the secondary resolution source.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast models from multiple sources converge on a daytime peak near 29°C for Munich on August 28, driven by southwesterly flow and modest daytime heating under partly cloudy skies, with afternoon scattered thunderstorms likely to increase cloud cover and limit further warming through evaporative cooling and reduced insolation. This places the outcome near or slightly above the long-term average high of 22.9°C while well below the August 28 record of 32.5°C. Market-implied odds clustering around 29–31°C reflect trader weighting of ensemble uncertainty in storm timing and intensity, which can shift the exact maximum by 1–2°C depending on whether convection develops before or after peak solar heating. Updated short-range guidance expected overnight will refine these probabilities ahead of resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast consensus points to a high of 23–25°C in Munich on August 29, 2026, as a cooler maritime air mass arrives from the west behind a weakening frontal system.** Multiple models, including ECMWF, ICON, and GFS runs valid as of August 27, show daytime maxima near 23–24°C under partly to mostly cloudy skies with light westerly flow and a modest chance of showers, limiting afternoon insolation compared with the warmer, sunnier conditions of August 27–28. This matches the historical late-August average high of ~22.8°C and explains why 24°C and 25°C together command roughly 72% of the market-implied probability.

**Key differentiating factors among the tightly bunched outcomes include the precise timing and extent of cloud cover and any embedded showers, which can suppress the daily maximum by 1–3°C.** Stronger or more persistent cloud decks, or earlier arrival of the cooler advection, favor the lower side (23–24°C), while brief clearing or slightly delayed frontal timing could allow brief peaks near 25–26°C. Ensemble spread remains modest at this 48-hour lead time, but small differences in boundary-layer moisture and wind direction near the Alps can shift the realized high within that narrow range. Updated model runs and official DWD guidance over the next 24 hours will provide the clearest signals ahead of market resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast models from the National Weather Service and private sources converge on a highest temperature near 82–84°F for New York City on August 28, 2026, consistent with the market’s top outcomes (82–83°F at 43.5%, 80–81°F at 23.5%, and 84–85°F at 22.5%).** Normal August highs average 82°F at Central Park, so today’s expected range sits close to climatology but with modest upward or downward variance driven by cloud cover and convection.

Key scientific drivers include a post-frontal airmass with west-to-northwest flow, reduced humidity after overnight clearing, and afternoon instability that supports a 30–40% chance of showers or thunderstorms. These storms can cap temperatures by limiting solar heating or allow brief spikes if they hold off until late in the day. Model consensus shows highs in the low-to-mid 80s across Central Park, LaGuardia, and JFK, with little spread between guidance runs issued late on August 27.

Recent developments reinforce this positioning: widespread severe thunderstorms on August 27 brought heavy rain and gusty winds that moistened the boundary layer but also cleared skies overnight, setting up partly sunny conditions for the 28th. No major heat ridge or tropical moisture plume is present to push values into the upper 80s or higher, keeping the probability of 86°F+ below 10%. Traders appear to weight the official NWS point forecasts and ensemble means most heavily, producing tight clustering around the 80–85°F bins while assigning negligible odds to extremes outside historical late-August variability.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 29 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=rjtt

If NOAA data is unavailable or missing for the observation period, Weather Underground will be used as the secondary resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecast updates from agencies like the Japan Meteorological Agency and international models indicate Tokyo will see increased cloud cover, scattered rain, and northeasterly flow on August 29, limiting daytime heating and supporting a maximum near 27–28°C. This follows hotter conditions earlier in the week, with ensemble guidance showing modest cooling from persistent moisture and reduced insolation rather than clear skies that could push readings toward 30°C or above. Historical climatology for late August favors highs near 31°C, but the current pattern aligns more closely with the lower end of recent runs, where model spread centers on the 26–29°C range. Traders are weighting the latest deterministic outputs and ensemble probabilities, which emphasize uncertainty around exact peak timing amid variable precipitation. Further model updates and official JMA briefings in the next 24 hours will refine these odds before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent official forecasts from the UK Met Office and European models point to a maximum of 20–22°C in London on August 29 under cloudy skies with periods of light rain and moderate southwesterly winds. These conditions, driven by an approaching Atlantic low-pressure system, suppress daytime heating and keep readings close to the late-August climatological average of roughly 21°C. Trader consensus, reflected in the 43.5% implied probability for 21°C and 25.5% for 20°C, aligns with this narrow forecast range, while lower odds for 22°C or higher reflect model agreement on limited insolation and potential for heavier showers. Updated guidance ahead of the 29th will be key for any shifts in these probabilities.

eventMetadata.context_description: Current National Weather Service and NOAA model guidance for New York City on August 29 points to a daily maximum in the upper 70s to low 80s, with ensemble spreads creating the tight market clustering around 78–83 °F. Key differentiating factors include variable afternoon cloud cover, boundary-layer moisture, and the strength of any onshore flow or weak frontal passage that could cap heating or enhance mixing. Late-August climatology shows a historical average high near 82 °F, yet recent model runs have trended slightly cooler, reflecting modest uncertainty in insolation and wind patterns. Traders are weighting the most probable range where forecast confidence is highest while discounting outliers beyond 84 °F that would require stronger high-pressure building or clearer skies than currently indicated.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast consensus from the Japan Meteorological Agency and other models points to a Tokyo high of 31–32°C on August 28, 2026, aligning with the market's heaviest weighting on those outcomes.** 

Cloudy skies with occasional scattered showers, driven by lingering summer monsoon moisture and southeasterly flow, are limiting daytime heating and keeping temperatures near the late-August climatological normal of ~30°C. Current observations show morning readings near 28–30°C under mostly cloudy conditions, with model runs indicating modest afternoon peaks unlikely to exceed 33°C absent a significant break in cloud cover. Recent forecast updates from August 27 have reinforced this moderate range rather than signaling intensification or suppression, supporting trader consensus around the 31–33°C band while assigning low probability to outliers above 34°C or below 31°C.

Typical late-August climatology for Central Park places the average daily maximum near 82°F, but the incoming high-pressure ridge and light winds (5–10 mph) limit further warming while clear conditions allow efficient daytime heating.

The tight clustering of market-implied probabilities around 78–81°F therefore reflects this narrow but still unresolved range, with lower odds on 82–83°F (16%) and minimal pricing for extremes above 84°F. **Forecast models and observational data indicate a peak temperature in Munich on August 28, 2026, most likely in the 29–31°C range, aligning closely with the market-implied probabilities (30°C at 46%, 31°C at 20.5%, 29°C at 19%).** Multiple sources, including WeatherBug (high near 29°C/85°F), Met Office (28°C), and others projecting 27–30°C, reflect warm air advection under partly cloudy skies early in the day, with daytime highs supported by solar heating before afternoon instability develops.

Key scientific drivers include moderate northwest winds, dew points around 15–18°C promoting efficient heating, and a frontal boundary or trough triggering scattered thunderstorms by midday or afternoon. These convective events—often linked to 50–80% precipitation probabilities in forecasts—increase cloud cover, enhance evaporative cooling, and disrupt surface heating, typically capping the daily maximum below the historical record of 32.5°C. Early observations on the day show temperatures climbing from ~18°C at dawn toward 26–28°C by midday, consistent with this trajectory.

Trader consensus, reflected in the tight clustering around 29–31°C, incorporates the latest model consensus (GFS/ECMWF runs) and real-time station data from Munich International Airport, where skin-in-the-game incentives favor accurate assessment of these meteorological thresholds over climatological averages (~23°C). Upcoming afternoon observations and any revised short-range forecasts could further refine resolution as storms evolve.

Historical analogs and model guidance prior to the date had already trended cooler amid a broader pattern of above-average precipitation for the month.

Realistic challenges to this positioning remain limited but could include a post-event data correction from the National Weather Service (rare for temperature maxima) or an unexpected resolution rule using a different station such as LaGuardia or JFK, where readings reached 79°F. Updated model guidance and surface observations through the afternoon remain the key near-term catalysts.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast consensus from multiple models positions 24–25°C as the most probable range for Munich’s maximum temperature on August 29, 2026.** Recent GFS and other numerical weather prediction runs indicate a high near 23–25°C (roughly 73–77°F) under mostly clear to partly cloudy afternoon conditions following overnight and morning showers. Westerly winds of 5–12 km/h and moderate humidity (around 45–60%) support gradual daytime warming without strong advection of warmer air masses.

This aligns with climatological norms: the 1991–2020 average high for the date is 22.8°C, with historical extremes ranging from 10.5°C to 33.0°C. Current steering patterns and post-frontal clearing after August 28 thunderstorms have tempered expectations for higher readings, while the absence of blocking highs or southerly flow keeps probabilities for 26°C or above low. Traders have weighted outcomes accordingly, with implied probabilities concentrated on the narrow 24–25°C band reflecting tight model agreement and limited forecast spread less than 24 hours before the observation window.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 30 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=rjtt

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency and international models indicate increased cloud cover, humidity, and scattered showers over Tokyo on August 30, suppressing daytime heating relative to seasonal norms of 31–32°C. This has shifted trader consensus toward 26–28°C highs, with 27°C holding the highest implied probability at 28% amid tight clustering. Key differentiating factors include variable low-level moisture advection, reduced insolation from stratiform clouds, and light northerly winds that limit mixing, all of which narrow the plausible range while leaving room for model adjustments if convective development intensifies or clears earlier than expected. Updated guidance ahead of the weekend will likely refine these probabilities.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecast updates from the German Weather Service and European models indicate Munich will likely peak near 28–30 °C on August 28 under partly cloudy skies with building instability. Afternoon thunderstorms and associated cloud cover, driven by a northwest flow and moderate humidity, are the dominant variables likely capping daytime maxima and explaining the market’s concentration around 29 °C. Real-time surface observations showing temperatures climbing through the mid-20s by late morning, combined with model consensus on convective initiation after 13:00 local time, underpin trader positioning. Higher outcomes above 31 °C would require delayed or weaker convection and stronger insolation, while lower readings hinge on earlier or heavier rainfall suppressing the thermal peak. Updated radar and model runs later today remain the key near-term catalysts.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent forecasts from the Met Office and other models indicate a maximum temperature of around 22°C for London on August 29, 2026, with widespread cloud cover, showers or rain, and southwesterly winds expected to limit daytime heating.** These conditions align with the market-implied probabilities favoring 20–21°C (combined ~76.5%), as persistent low-level cloud and precipitation reduce solar insolation and suppress the diurnal temperature rise typical for late summer.

Scientific drivers include an unsettled Atlantic flow bringing mild but moist air masses, with forecast soundings showing limited instability and boundary-layer mixing capped by stratiform clouds. Historical climatology for late August in London shows mean daily maxima near 20–22°C, and current model consensus (Met Office, ECMWF guidance reflected in public outputs) shows no strong ridging or clear-sky subsidence that would push readings to 23°C or higher. The low odds on 22°C+ reflect this consensus, while probabilities cluster around 20–21°C because showers are timed to coincide with peak heating hours, preventing full realization of the 22°C guidance in many ensemble members.

Traders are weighting the latest model runs showing rain probabilities exceeding 50–70% midday onward, which introduces downward bias relative to clear-sky potential. Upcoming updates from the Met Office and high-resolution models will likely refine the exact peak once radar and satellite trends confirm cloud thickness and shower timing.

Observed trends through August 28 show similar moderation from cloud cover and precipitation, with official guidance highlighting 50–60% rain chances during peak heating hours that could further cap temperatures. Updated JMA briefings and short-range model consensus expected later today represent the next key data points that could shift resolution thresholds around the 26–29°C band.

The climatological average high for August 29 is 81.3°F, and current model guidance (including NWS tabular forecasts) clusters tightly around 80–82°F, with limited upside risk from cloud cover or southerly return flow until later in the weekend.

Traders appear to be weighting the most probable narrow band (78–79°F at 54.5%) slightly below the raw forecast mean while assigning meaningful probability to the adjacent 80–81°F bin, reflecting typical uncertainty in the final model runs and the exact maximum observation time. Lower-probability outcomes (82°F+) would require unexpected southerly advection or reduced mixing, scenarios not supported by current guidance.

Low precipitation probability (under 20% in most guidance) and dew points in the low teens Celsius reduce latent heat effects that could suppress the maximum. Traders' heavy weighting toward 25°C (63.5%) reflects the tight clustering of deterministic and ensemble guidance around this value, with 24°C and 26°C as plausible outliers depending on exact boundary-layer mixing and any residual moisture. New model runs or observational data from Munich stations in the next 12–24 hours could refine this before resolution.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 30 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the LaGuardia Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 29 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=klga

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

**Official forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency and supporting models project a maximum of 31–32°C for Tokyo on August 28 under cloudy skies with scattered showers and 40–60% precipitation chances, aligning with the market's 99.7% implied probability for 32°C.** 

This positioning reflects August climatology (normal daily high near 31°C) and recent model consensus showing limited daytime heating due to persistent cloud cover and moisture. Real-time observations during the day have hovered near or slightly above forecast values without exceeding the 32°C threshold. 

A realistic challenge would require unexpected clearing and stronger insolation, but current steering patterns and moisture make significant upside unlikely before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast consensus from the Japan Meteorological Agency and aligned numerical models points to a Tokyo daily maximum of 32°C on August 28, 2026, under mostly cloudy skies with scattered showers and light southerly winds.** 

This aligns with climatological norms for late August (historical averages near 31°C) and real-time observations showing temperatures climbing into the low 30s amid high humidity and limited solar heating from cloud cover. Trader positioning at near-100% implied probability for exactly 32°C reflects this strong model agreement and the resolution criteria tied to official JMA station data. 

A realistic challenge would require stronger-than-expected convective rainfall or a sharper drop in insolation during peak heating hours, though current guidance shows low odds of such a shift before the daily high is recorded.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 29 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=rjtt

If NOAA data is unavailable or missing for the observation period, Weather Underground will be used as the secondary resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Cloud cover, widespread showers, and a maritime air mass are capping daytime heating in Tokyo on August 29, 2026, driving strong trader consensus toward a daily maximum near 27°C (82.5% implied probability).**

Official Japan Meteorological Agency guidance and multiple numerical models forecast a high of 27–29°C under persistent overcast skies and periods of rain, with precipitation probabilities of 30–60% through the afternoon. This setup reduces incoming solar radiation and enhances evaporative cooling, preventing the surface from reaching the 31–33°C readings observed on August 28. Historical late-August climatology shows typical maxima near 30–31°C under clearer conditions; the current pattern deviates due to an active frontal boundary or remnant tropical moisture that favors stratiform clouds and light northeasterly flow.

Model agreement remains tight on these thresholds, with limited upside risk to 28–29°C only if partial clearing occurs earlier than expected. Downside scenarios below 26°C appear improbable given the warm, humid boundary layer. With resolution imminent, fresh model runs and JMA updates overnight represent the primary near-term catalysts that could still shift marginal probabilities around the 27–28°C boundary.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Persistent cloud cover, widespread rain, and southwesterly flow are the dominant drivers keeping the highest temperature in London on 29 August tightly clustered around 20–21 °C in trader consensus.** Official guidance from the Met Office and supporting model output (GFS/ECMWF consensus) projects a maximum of 21 °C under overcast skies with rain, occasionally heavy or thundery, moving across the region during the morning and lingering through much of the day. This matches the market’s leading probabilities: 21 °C at 39.5 % and 20 °C at 32.5 %.

The key scientific factors differentiating these closely matched outcomes are the timing and intensity of cloud breaks and precipitation. Thick stratiform cloud and high relative humidity (often 80–90 %) sharply reduce incoming solar radiation, limiting surface heating. Evaporative cooling from rain further caps the daily peak, while moderate southwesterly winds (10–15 mph) promote mixing that prevents localized warm pockets. Any earlier clearance or lighter rainfall could allow brief insolation to push readings to 22 °C (14.5 % probability), whereas heavier or more prolonged showers would favor 19 °C (13.5 %). Higher outcomes (23 °C+) remain low-probability because the unsettled pattern shows little sign of significant model divergence or rapid clearing before peak heating hours. Traders are therefore pricing the most likely range based on the latest observational data and forecast consensus rather than historical August averages.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Met Office and ensemble forecasts indicate a maximum of around 22°C for London on August 30, driven by southwesterly flow advecting mild maritime air under variable cloud cover with light showers possible midday. These conditions limit peak solar insolation and surface heating compared to clearer anticyclonic setups, while dew points near 14–15°C support modest instability without widespread convection. Model runs show close agreement on daily highs in the low 20s Celsius, consistent with the 1991–2020 climatological average of 22°C for the date, though minor shifts in cloud timing or wind gusts could nudge the observed peak between 21°C and 23°C. Traders weight 22°C and 23°C most heavily as fresh guidance narrows the range ahead of resolution.

Forecasts from sources like WeatherBug, globalmeteo, and Yr.no cluster in the 79–80°F (26–27°C) range, above the late-August climatological average high of ~22.6°C but well below historical extremes near 33°C. Minor model spread around cloud cover and exact timing of any weak fronts creates the tight clustering on 26–28°C, with traders weighting recent ensemble guidance heavily as the short-term window narrows. Updated runs from major centers will likely refine probabilities before resolution.

This reflects a typical late-August pattern shift rather than seasonal norms around 31°C, driven by northerly or northeasterly flow and high humidity that limits solar insolation.

Recent data show the highest probabilities clustering tightly around 27°C because forecast runs emphasize steady rain chances (70–100% in some models) and minimal diurnal temperature rise, reducing the odds of reaching 29°C or higher to under 5% combined. Traders appear to weigh the consensus on cooler, unsettled conditions more heavily than any potential brief clearing that could push readings modestly higher. Resolution hinges on the official Japan Meteorological Agency maximum at a standard Tokyo station; upcoming model updates or radar trends could refine the exact value but are unlikely to shift the outcome far outside the 26–28°C window.

gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Tokyo on August 30?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 30 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=rjtt

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecast consensus from agencies like the Japan Meteorological Agency and international models points to mostly cloudy skies with limited precipitation and light northerly winds on August 30, supporting daytime highs near 27–28°C after cooler, rainier conditions on the 28th–29th. These temperatures align with late-August climatology for Tokyo, where urban heat island effects and variable cloud cover can shift maxima by 1–2°C depending on solar radiation and boundary-layer mixing. Traders appear to weigh the balance between partial clearing that could push readings toward 29°C against lingering moisture that favors the lower end, with new model runs expected to refine steering patterns and diurnal temperature ranges ahead of market resolution.
